title: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Heritage Listing for the Bight) Bill 2019
short_title: Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Heritage Listing for the Bight) Bill 2019

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require the Environment Minister to place a defined Great Australian Bight heritage area on the National Heritage List and record its heritage values.
It would establish a special listing process requiring consultation with affected Western Australian and South Australian communities before the Minister includes heritage values for the area.
The bill would begin on royal assent and cover the specified Southern Ocean area within Australia’s continental shelf, excluding areas belonging to external territories.
changes: The Minister would have to publish the listing instrument in the Gazette.
The listed values could include heritage values the Minister considers the area may possess.
The heritage area could not subsequently be removed from the National Heritage List.
summary.affected: Communities in South Australia and Western Australia likely to be affected by the listing, and the Environment Minister, are affected.

speeches.speaker: Rebekha Sharkie
speeches.brief: The member moved the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Heritage Listing for the Bight) Bill 2019, arguing that national heritage listing would protect the Great Australian Bight from the catastrophic risks of deep-sea oil drilling by Equinor, and that a full ban is preferred but this bill is a reasonable first step.
